To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the magnetic field increases the critical temperature of the chiral phase transition and that the pion decay and the chiral condensate decrease slower with the temperature in a magnetic field as compared to vanishing magnetic field.

(i) the pion thermal mass and the pion mass splitting increase as a function of the magnetic field, (ii) the pion decay-constant splitting and the quark- condensate splitting decrease as a function of T, (iii) the quark condensation temperature Tc increases as a function of magnetic field.

the magnetic field increases the critical temperature T c for the chiral symmetry restoration and that the pion decay and the quark chiral condensates are decreasing slower as functions of T in the presence of magnetic field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the influence of a constant external magnetic field on the thermodynamic properties of the pions.
the study of the effects of a constant magnetic background on the chiral transition in the SU(2)-flavor sector.
the effects of the magnetic field on the chiral transition in the SU(2) sector of QCD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic field has a tendency to stabilize the chiral symmetry.
the lattice calculations are not yet in agreement with chiral perturbation calculations.
the effect of the magnetic field on the chiral condensate and the pion mass is not well understood yet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic field has a significant influence on the chiral transition.
the chiral transition becomes smoother in a magnetic field.
chiral perturbation at finite temperature in a constant magnetic field gives a qualitatively correct description of the magnetic catalysis effect, but that the quantitative agreement is poor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetic field induces a splitting between M π0 and M π ± and between F π0 and F π ±.
the chiral transition in the presence of magnetic fields is more robust than in the absence of magnetic fields.
the pion masses and decay constants in a constant magnetic field are different from the case of zero magnetic field.
